I reviewed quite extensively this code in the past cycle and I'm confident the overall architecture is sound. The code will need more inspection, and I will obviously do a final pass for due diligence later before approving.
That said, concerns were raised about code duplication and I think there's a way to address these avoiding massive rewrites and retaining the full path independence.
The key insight is to unify the interface while keep the implementation path separated (actually the resize path will partially reuse the base path, but that's fine: it's a form of additive change).

The key idea is to push the differences in ForResize variants of the cpuAccumulator, numaOrSocketFirstFuncs and sortCPUs*.
After that, we can and should move the new code in a `_resize.go` and `_resize_test.go` files, so it's very obvious the base path is unchanged and all the new code is additive, so the chances of breaking the existing path is much, much lower and also the changes are easier to review (at this layer at least).

I implemented a possible approach in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/81e428f576f01cca493b5e249dab13eba43461fc

Then, we can remove quite some of the trivial one-line code forwarding functions adding an embedded struct with function pointers: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/1a0e300a199a53707f7015f9f970c6b176978508

should you adopt any of these changes (please do consider them), no need to cite or quote or add co-authorship as these are trivial code movement and reshaping, not much to credit for.
Also note comments may be obsolete or miscopied.
